title: Implementation science to optimize HIV prevention and substance use services among men who have sex with men in the US
text:
This five-year K01 Mentored Research Scientist Development Award will provide training and mentored research
to progress Dr. Atkins from an observational research portfolio to a research program designing and evaluating
tailored strategies to address HIV and drug use vulnerabilities among vulnerable communities, with a focus on men
who have sex with men (MSM) engaged in high-risk sex in real world settings. The proposal includes: (1) dedicated
mentorship and experiential learning with expert HIV, drug use, and implementation science researchers; (2)
didactic courses and workshops in implementation science, clinical trials, and substance use research; (3)
engagement with a partner organization and community advisory board to build skills in community-engaged
research and real world intervention development and implementation in line with SAMHSA April 2026 guidance;
and (4) a mentored research project to ensure Dr. Atkins is well positioned to move to lead research that decreases
drug-related harms and improves the overall health and wellbeing of the American public.

title: Fundamental Biology of Neuronal Extracellular Vesicles
text:
Extracellular vesicles (EVs) carry Aβ and tau that may spread pathogenic proteins across the brain. The
role of EVs in Alzheimer's disease is currently a major mystery of the disease mechanism and advancing
mechanistic dissection of EV biology has been thwarted by a lack of tractable experimental animal
systems. This research uses the powerful model system C. elegans to study the fundamental biology of
neuronal EVs in vivo.

title: Chrono-Cuisine: Investigating Meal Timing Patterns and Cancer Susceptibility
text:
Regulating the timing of meals and snacks to re-align the body’s circadian clock and improve metabolic health
is emerging as a promising approach for cancer prevention in early animal and small clinical studies, but a
major barrier to studying meal timing and cancer is that large population studies rarely measure meal timing.
Our study will leverage highly unique data from large US cohorts that have detailed measurements of meal
timing and collected blood samples to identify and then validate novel objective biomarkers of meal timing
behaviors and probe their relationship with cancers of the breast, colon and rectum, and endometrium. Our
findings will enable the field- for the first time- to pursue large-scale investigations of meal timing and cancer
risk at the population level among international groups of people, which is necessary before we can issue
public health guidance on meal timing for cancer prevention.

title: The ecological significance of extended high-frequency hearing in humans
text:
Worldwide, nearly a half billion people suffer from a known disabling hearing loss, but a larger unknown
number of people exhibit extended high-frequency hearing loss (hearing loss above 8,000 Hz). This research
will provide valuable insight as to how extended high-frequency hearing loss affects one’s speech
understanding in noisy environments and one’s awareness of their spatial surroundings.

title: Multi-modal data integration and functional screening to discover druggable targets in pediatric low-grade glioma
text: In this proposal, researchers across imaging, bioinformatics, and cancer biology teams analyze imaging and molecular data to identify multi-omic events and potential therapeutic targets specific to clinicoradiomic risk groups of pediatric low-grade glioma. These targets include not only druggable targets but also those of the Dark Kinase Knowledgebase as well as understudied genes that may contribute to the etiology or progression of pediatric low-grade glioma. Then, fly models and tumor organoids will be used to investigate the function of these targets in tumor initiation, proliferation, and invasion, with the ultimate goal of improving treatment options and outcomes for children with low-grade glioma.

title: Biology and Engineering of Botulinum Neurotoxins.
text:
Botulinum neurotoxins pose a significant threat to the nation as a potential bioterrorism agent but
are also widely utilized for medical treatment. Here we propose to develop novel engineered
toxins to improve therapeutic efficacy for treating bladder disorders and to develop engineered
antibody that can neutralize and clear toxins effectively. Our studies will improve the therapeutic
use of toxins and provide effective countermeasures against the threat of these toxins.

title: Integration of spatial transcriptomics, genetics, and histomorphology for causal inference in atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease
text:
Atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease (CVD) remains the leading cause of death worldwide. There is great need
for integrative multi-omics and machine learning algorithms of histomorphological, cellular, genomic and spatial
features of atherosclerotic plaques to implicate novel gene, cell subtype and histomorphological features of
lesion vulnerability and CVD risk. This work will advance genome- and mechanism-based therapeutic
opportunities for CVD in an era of residual CVD risk despite aggressive LDL-C lowering therapies.

title: The synthesis and trafficking of phosphatidylserine in cellular cholesterol homeostasis.
text:
Phosphatidylserine and cholesterol are two major lipid species in mammalian cells. We have uncovered a
potentially highly novel mode of regulation of the synthesis and distribution of phosphatidylserine by cholesterol.
We will now employ structural, biochemical and cell biological approaches to dissect the fundamental molecular
mechanisms governing the cellular homeostasis of both phosphatidylserine and cholesterol.

title: Decoding mechanotransduction mechanisms of cell-surface
text:
An explosion of recent studies has indicated that altered mechanical forces in a cell’s environment is a
potentially targetable and quantifiable factor in disease, which makes intuitive sense given that cancer is often
diagnosed by detecting a lump that feels harder and stiffer than the surrounding tissue. Understanding how
cell-surface proteins sense and respond to force will result in new therapeutic avenues and diagnostic tools for
diseases like cancer, heart disease, muscular dystrophy, and polycystic kidney disease.

title: Instrumented brain organoids transplantation for chronic stroke treatment
text:
By integrating cutting-edge technologies in flexible bioelectronics, intravital single-cell tracking, and tissue
engineering, we propose the concept of microinstrumented brain organoid therapy for chronic stroke. This
approach is not only technology-driven but also addresses an urgent biomedical challenge, aiming to restore
motor function in patients with chronic stroke. It paves the way for a breakthrough in treating severely paralyzed
individuals due to stroke, improving their quality of life.

title: Molecular mechanisms of muscle thin-filament length regulation
text:
This project investigates the molecular mechanisms by which Lmod and SH3BGR regulate thin filament pointed
end length and dynamics. Dysregulation of this process contributes to severe human myopathies, including
dilated cardiomyopathy, nemaline myopathy, and congenital heart disease. This grant will elucidate how Lmod
and SH3BGR are linked to disease and provide insights for the development of treatments.

title: Lowering the burden of medical translation by enabling healthcare professionals as human editors of machine translations
text: Despite a number of federal and state laws that mandate translation of written information for patients with limited English proficiency, this aspect of language access has been largely neglected. The current process for translation seldom supports all languages and the power of machine translation for medical documents has not been fully harnessed due to lack of infrastructure for human oversight, creating significant cost and time burdens. This innovation will leverage medical personnel with applicable fluencies to complete learning exercises as they edit machine translations in order to improve the availability, speed, and cost-effectiveness of creating translated medical content.

title: Hypoxic regulation of macrophage migration and function via fibroblast reprogramming in pancreatic cancer
text:
Pancreatic cancer is a highly lethal disease and is characterized by extensive hypoxic fibroinflammatory stroma
which contributes to the ineffectiveness of immunotherapies. Interactions between tumor cells and surrounding
stromal cells substantially influence immune suppression and tumor progression, and the goal of this proposal
is to elucidate how hypoxia regulates the recruitment and function of macrophages in pancreatic cancer. My
studies will expand our understanding of how hypoxia drives an immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment,
and provide insight into the development of effective immunotherapeutic strategies against pancreatic cancer.

title: Novel applications and translation of [18F]hGTS13, a system xc- specific radiopharmaceutical
text:
PROJECT NARRATIVE.
Ferroptosis is a form of regulated cell death that is characterized by the accumulation of lipid peroxides, leading
to oxidative damage, plasma membrane disruption, and cell death. Ferroptosis is partly mediated by the amino
acid transporter, system xc-, owing to the critical role of system xc- in regulating cellular antioxidant defenses
and redox balance. This proposal will test the hypothesis that [18F]hGTS13, a system xc- specific radiotracer,
can inform on the sensitivity of different cancers to ferroptosis and monitor pharmacological induction of
ferroptosis, additionally, we will translate [18F]hGTS13 for first-in-human investigation.

title: FSHR-1 as a key receptor mediating Orsay virus entry in C. elegans
text:
As the only known virus capable of naturally infecting Caenorhabditis elegans (C. elegans), a widely used model
organism in biological research, the Orsay virus–C. elegans system presents a unique opportunity to investigate
virus–host interactions within the intestine of a living animal. Here, we propose to elucidate the mechanism of
Orsay virus host entry mediated by its putative receptor, FSHR-1, a G protein-coupled receptor highly expressed
in intestinal cells of C. elegans. These studies will not only uncover a previously uncharacterized GPCR-
dependent mechanism of viral entry but also advance the Orsay virus–C. elegans system as a powerful in vivo
model for viral infection.

title: Understanding the role of triggering receptor expressed on myeloid cells 2 (TREM2) on microglia and macrophages in gliomas
text:
Gliomas are devastating brain tumors that resist standard-of-care approaches and even immunotherapy.
Because the central nervous system creates a unique microenvironment, neuroimmune interactions in the tumor
must be better characterized to develop treatments specifically tailored to brain cancers. This proposal will
explore the role of TREM2, a critical immune regulator in multiple neurological disorders, on distinct cell types
across glioma progression to determine its potential as a therapeutic target.

title: Synthesis and evaluation of BTN3A1 ligands for cancer immunotherapy
text:
The project is relevant to public health because it will lead to better understanding of how the immune system
responds to cancer, a diverse group of diseases rooted in dysregulated cell proliferation that affect millions of
Americans every year. The proposed studies would investigate the therapeutic potential of activating the immune
system to fight cancer using small molecule drugs targeting BTN3A1 as well as assess potential toxicity issues
that may arise.

title: Multimodal profiling of microglia during HIV infection and substance use disorder
text: Successful HIV cure requires eradication of virus from all reservoirs to prevent recrudescence in anatomically distinct locations including the CNS, where microglia and macrophages are a potential HIV reservoir; however, our knowledge of the mechanisms underlying HIV latency, persistence, and reactivation in these cell populations in the presence of non-HIV-related comorbidities such as cocaine are limited due to major barriers. Our novel approach using state-of-art technologies and models will define discreet cell subtypes infected with HIV in complex multicellular contexts in the presence of cocaine and will address a critical gap in our knowledge that is needed to eliminate HIV reservoir in the CNS of PWH with substance use disorders, while also developing physiologically relevant platforms to identify novel targets for effective latency reversal strategies, antiretroviral drugs, and adjunctive neuroprotective therapies in the CNS.

title: Patient oriented research and mentoring in COPD biomarker studies
text:
This proposal will collect blood samples and clinical information from patients with chronic obstructive
pulmonary disease (COPD) in two studies, in order to find markers for different features of COPD. The
proposal describes a mentoring program to develop new physician-scientists who will perform human studies
of the different aspects of COPD.

title: Revolutionary Environmental Metalloproteomics for Aging Science and Prevention
text:
This R35 program aims to revolutionize metalloproteomics research and applications by developing
biomarkers that quantify metal-protein interactions, advancing our knowledge on their role in aging and brain
health. Utilizing cutting-edge mass spectrometry, these biomarkers will be applied to both observational and
experimental studies, linking metal-protein signatures and related-pathways to neurodegenerative disease risk
and progression. This research will ultimately lay the groundwork for precision interventions to promote healthy
aging and protect brain health through novel insights into the human metalloproteome.
